verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents an OS-level sandbox (Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) that limits what the agent and its child processes can read, write and reach on the network. It also offers isolated worktree sessions, file-restoring checkpoints, and deny rules for dangerous commands. Together these let an agent run and test without reaching production resources. However, all of this is local process and workspace isolation; nothing describes a dedicated sandbox or test environment with non-production data to test against. missing for 10: a documented sandbox/test environment with mock or non-production data, guidance on configuring sandbox network rules to block production endpoints, independent hands-on corroboration of the sandbox.
